purpose: deliver a feature across interface, service and data in one coherent change, without leaving the seams untested
entry_criteria: The feature is described end to end with acceptance criteria
Front-end and back-end contracts are defined
The whole stack runs locally or in an ephemeral environment
procedure: Agree the contract between interface and service first; use it to build both sides in parallel against stubs.
Implement the thinnest working path from interface to data, then add cases and error handling.
Keep state and validation consistent on both sides; the server stays the authority.
Test across the seam with at least one end-to-end test of the main path plus unit tests on each side.
Check the user experience for loading, empty, error and slow states, and accessibility basics.
Release behind a feature flag when the change is risky, with a documented way to turn it off.
deliverables: contract and tests on both sides
acceptance_criteria: The main path works end to end
Error, empty and loading states are handled
The server validates everything the client validates
A switch-off path exists for risky features
validation_method: Code review and product owner demonstration.

validation.command: pytest -q tests/api && npx --no-install playwright test tests/e2e/feature.spec.ts   # example

validation.check: switch the feature flag off and confirm the old behavior returns

failure_modes.detection: Server rejects what the client allowed
failure_modes.response: Make the server the authority and share the schema

failure_modes.detection: Flag missing for a risky change

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A saved-search feature adds a save button, an API endpoint and a table. The contract is agreed first; one end-to-end test saves and reloads a search, and a flag allows hiding the button without a deployment.
